transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-11-09 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 min
- Recorder: Fireflies.ai
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Alex (Halcyon Platform), Jenna (Halcyon InfoSec), Samir (Data Eng), Li (Product), Tom (Legal)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot security results: audit logs, SSO integration gaps, data retention behavior observed in staging, SOC2 evidence ask and next steps for a short handoff to Procurement. Agreed to run one additional retention/export test and schedule IdP deep dive.

Topics: SSO/SAML + SCIM, audit log fidelity, log retention and export, SOC2 docs, KMS and encryption at rest, RBAC model, demo requests, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out the time. We'll take about 45 minutes and save 10 for any legal questions. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Alex: Alex here.
[00:13] Jenna: Jenna.
[00:15] Samir: Samir.
[00:16] Li: Li.
[00:18] Tom: Tom.
[00:20] Connor: Connor here.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: review the security findings from the pilot runs, go over the SSO work and scim, show the audit-log sample output, and agree next steps.
[00:33] Jenna: Sounds good. We got the first batch of logs you dropped last week, I had a quick skim, a couple of misses where usernames came in as email vs uid. Not sure if that's on our side or the mapping.
[00:45] Connor: Right, that was expected. The staging IdP (we used their short-lived assertion) had the email attribute labelled differently. We've got a mapping flag in config but it wasn't enabled in your staging env, so the logs show the raw payload. We can normalize that on ingest.
[01:05] Samir: If you normalize, can you also add the device/agent string? Our SIEM team needs that surface to tie sessions.
[01:12] Connor: We capture user-agent at request time but not always at the token refresh event. We can add the refresh event to the audit stream. That will increase log volume though, FYI.
[01:25] Jenna: Volume is a concern - retention costs are part of why we're evaluating dedicated vs hosted. What did you see for per-day log growth in the pilot?
[01:34] Priya: From our end, default audit verbosity pushed about ~120MB/day for the test workload (50k tokens/day), with token-cache events off. With cache + batching on it's down to ~30-40MB/day.
[01:47] Li: That's useful. For compliance we need 365 days of logs, at least metadata, correct?
[01:52] Tom: Our baseline SOC2 asks for one year of immutable logs and evidence of access controls. We'll want to see if Redwood supports WORM-like retention or an export that we can ship to our archive.
[02:07] Maya: Yes, currently we support both: retention policies at the tenant level and an export pipeline to an S3 bucket or your SIEM using syslog/forwarder. For short-term, we can enable an export job that runs daily with gzipped JSON.
[02:22] Alex: How about encryption keys? We need customer-managed keys (CMK) option.
[02:28] Connor: We support KMS integration. For hosted we offer an envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and CMK via AWS KMS or an HSM for Dedicated/Private. There are perf tradeoffs on key rotation; we can document the latency impact.
[02:45] Jenna: And audit log integrity? Any signing?
[02:49] Connor: We provide SHA256 signing on export bundles; we can add a signed manifest per day. For higher assurance, we can stream to your SIEM which already has append-only storage.
[03:02] Samir: Regarding SSO, our IdP has SCIM for user provisioning. We tried a sync, user creation worked but groups weren't mapped.
[03:12] Maya: That's likely attribute mapping. We'll coordinate a SCIM mapping session. Connor, can we confirm scim groupMapping is in the 1.2 branch?
[03:20] Connor: Yes, groupMapping shipped in 1.2 but requires an admin toggle. We didn't ship that toggle to your staging tenant automatically because of potential mapping surprises. We'll flip it in staging and run a dry-run.
[03:35] Jenna: Can you do a dry-run and show the payload so our IdP engineer can validate?
[03:40] Connor: Absolutely. I'll post the sample payload and the curl we used to the shared drive.
[03:46] Li: On retention, how easy is it to pull historical transcripts for specific queries? We need to show a chain of custody if an incident happens.
[03:55] Priya: We keep an index for event timestamps and object ids; search is supported but for long-term archiving we recommend exporting daily snapshots to your archive. The search UI can query 90 days by default in hosted, longer for Dedicated.
[04:12] Jenna: If we go Dedicated, can we configure a 7-year retention for logs?
[04:18] Maya: Yes, Dedicated gives you full control of retention and export. The tradeoff is storage costs and lifecycle management; we can propose lifecycle rules to tier older logs to cheaper storage.
[04:30] Alex: Any blockers left for SOC2 evidence? We asked for a SOC2 summary and bridge letter.
[04:36] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 summary and a bridge letter this week. Also we can provide the penetration test report redacted and our security architecture diagram.
[04:45] Tom: We need a list of subservice organizations if any. Also want to confirm data residency options for EU.
[04:51] Connor: We have region pins for data at rest; for hosted we have eu-west and us-east. Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC in EU region. We'll include the deployment topology doc.
[05:05] Jenna: A point on logs: when you export gzipped bundles, are the individual event timestamps preserved (millisecond precision)? Our SIEM relies on that.
[05:12] Connor: Yes milliseconds preserved. The gzips contain newline-delimited JSON with an event_ts field in ISO8601 with milliseconds.
[05:20] Samir: Great. For the upcoming test, we'll want to simulate a retention deletion and see the export still return the previous days - basically test the export pipeline against deletion.
[05:30] Connor: We can run that scenario in staging: create events day 0, run export day 1, then run deletion and verify the archive contains the day 0 bundle. I'll be explicit in the test plan.
[05:40] Jenna: Also curious about RBAC: can we scope token permissions down to product area? We want to ensure dev teams only see their routes.
[05:48] Maya: Yes, we support role-based policies with route-level scopes and model scoping. For Dedicated you'll get finer-grained provisioning with SCIM group to role mapping.
[05:58] Li: Any perf impacts when enabling audit verbosity to include request/response hashes?
[06:04] Connor: Minimal CPU overhead for hashing, roughly +3-5% p99 latency in our synthetic tests. It adds some I/O to the audit stream which affects storage. We'll include benchmark numbers.
[06:18] Tom: On legal, we may need a DPA addendum and to confirm subprocessors.
[06:23] Maya: We'll attach the DPA and subprocessors list to the packet we send; legal can review with your team.
[06:29] Alex: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[06:32] Maya: Connor will run the retention/export test and post logs by 11/16. I'll send SOC2 summary + bridge letter and pricing by 11/12. Priya will drop the SSO/SCIM runbook and the sample payload by 11/13. We'll schedule SCIM mapping joint session week of 11/22.
[06:49] Jenna: Sounds good. Quick Q: competitor question, we ran a small test comparing log volumes vs GigaAI and saw similar numbers but GigaAI pushed more metadata. Any way to tune off those fields?
[07:01] Connor: Yes, we have configurable audit fields; we can produce a slim profile with only essentials and a verbose profile with full context.
[07:12] Samir: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:15] Tom: Not from legal. We'll wait for your docs.
[07:18] Li: Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
